blocks.h2: Sewer Backup Questions From McHenry Homeowners

items.q: Why does my basement drain back up when the river is high?
items.preview: Saturated ground and full sewers push water to the lowest point.
items.answer: When the ground is saturated and sewers are carrying more water, the lowest opening in your plumbing, usually the floor drain, is where it shows up. A backflow valve or overhead sewer keeps it out.

items.q: How do I know if it's my line or the city's?
items.preview: A camera inspection shows where the blockage is.
items.answer: We clear the line and camera it. If the blockage is in your line, it's on the private side. If your line is clear and the sewer is overloaded, it's on the public side.

items.q: Can I clean up a sewer backup myself?
items.preview: Small spills on concrete, carefully. Larger ones need professionals.
items.answer: A small spill on bare concrete can be cleaned with gloves and disinfectant. Anything reaching carpet, drywall or furniture needs a professional cleanup company.

items.q: How do I stop it from happening again?
items.preview: Fix the cause and add protection.
items.answer: Fix what caused it, then protect the basement. Regular [sewer cleaning](/mchenry/sewer-maintenance) and a backflow valve or [overhead sewer](/mchenry/overhead-sewer-systems) cover most cases.

items.q: Can a full septic tank cause a basement backup?
items.answer: Yes. If your home is on septic and the tank is full, wastewater backs up into the lowest drains. We'll check the line and tell you if the tank needs pumping.

items.q: How much does sewer backup service cost in McHenry?
items.preview: It depends on the cause. You get a flat price first.
items.answer: It depends on what caused the backup and how we reach the line. We give you a flat-rate price before any work begins.
